script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Romance
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

EXT. MORNING - SMALL TOWN - MAIN STREET

Sun rises over a quaint little town, morning mist blanketing the ground. The sound of birds singing fills the air.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(voiceover)
In the heart of the Midwest, nestled between rolling hills and towering cornfields, lies the town of Wellington.

EXT. MAIN STREET - DAY

A bustling main street with shops opening up for the day. People greet each other warmly as they pass by.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

JESSICA, 28, a local artist, sits at a table, sketching in her notebook. LUCAS, 31, a teacher, enters, carrying a cup of coffee.

LUCAS
(cheerfully)
Morning, Jessica.

JESSICA
(looking up)
Good morning, Lucas.

They share a smile as Lucas takes a seat across from her.

SCENE 2 - THE LIBRARY

INT. LIBRARY - DAY

Jessica and Lucas sit at a table, surrounded by books. They discuss literature and art.

LUCAS
(passionately)
You know, some people say that art is a window to the soul. What do you think?

JESSICA
(smiling)
I believe that's true. Art is a powerful means of expressing emotions and connecting with others.

SCENE 3 - THE PARK

EXT. PARK - AFTERNOON

Jessica and Lucas enjoy a picnic in the park. They share stories about their pasts and dreams for the future.

JESSICA
(laughing)
I've never met anyone quite like you, Lucas.

LUCAS
(blushing)
And I feel the same way about you, Jessica.

They share a moment of silence, watching the sun set over the park.

SCENE 4 - ART GALLERY

INT. ART GALLERY - NIGHT

Jessica shows Lucas her artwork at an exhibit. He is moved by her creations and expresses his admiration.

JESSICA
(emotional)
Thank you, Lucas. This means so much to me.

LUCAS
(sincerely)
You deserve all the success in the world.

They share a tender kiss amidst the silence of the gallery.

SCENE 5 - THE BAKERY

INT. BAKERY - MORNING

Jessica and Lucas enjoy a breakfast pastry and conversation.

JESSICA
(smiling)
I feel so lucky to have you in my life, Lucas.

LUCAS
(grinning)
And I feel the same way about you, Jessica.

SCENE 6 - LUCAS'S CLASSROOM

INT. SCHOOL - DAY

Lucas teaches a class about the importance of art in education. He shares Jessica's artwork as an example.

SCENE 7 - JESSICA'S STUDIO

INT. ART STUDIO - EVENING

Jessica works on a new piece, inspired by Lucas and their growing relationship.

SCENE 8 - THE FARMER'S MARKET

EXT. FARMER'S MARKET - DAY

Jessica and Lucas stroll through the market, purchasing fresh produce and sharing stories with locals.

SCENE 9 - COOKING TOGETHER

INT. KITCHEN - EVENING

Jessica and Lucas cook dinner together, enjoying each other's company and sharing cooking tips.

SCENE 10 - THE MOVIE THEATER

INT. MOVIE THEATER - NIGHT

Jessica and Lucas attend a showing of their favorite romantic comedy, laughing and holding hands throughout the film.

SCENE 11 - WALKING DOWN MAIN STREET

EXT. MAIN STREET - NIGHT

Jessica and Lucas take a leisurely stroll down Main Street, admiring the twinkling lights and holiday decorations.

SCENE 12 - SNOWBALL FIGHT

EXT. SNOWFALL - NIGHT

Jessica and Lucas engage in a playful snowball fight, leaving them both laughing and covered in snow.

SCENE 13 - THE TOWN SQUARE

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - NIGHT

Jessica and Lucas sit on a bench in the town square, gazing up at the stars and sharing dreams for the future.

SCENE 14 - NEW YEAR'S EVE

EXT. TOWN SQUARE - NIGHT

Jessica and Lucas ring in the new year with a kiss, surrounded by the warmth and love of their small town.

SCENE 15 - A YEAR LATER

EXT. MAIN STREET - MORNING

The sun rises over the town of Wellington, casting a warm glow on the couple as they sit on the porch of their newly renovated house.

NARRATOR (V.O.)
(voiceover)
And so, love bloomed in the heart of Wellington, reminding us all that even in the smallest of towns, the biggest adventures can be found.

FADE OUT.
